title: Deliverability readiness: DMARC template, simulator tests, pause drill, dead letters, warm-up
description:
**Goal.** Before any reader signup opens, sending is proven safe: authentication aligned, failure paths exercised, reputation warmed, pause working. All sites share one SES account reputation, so one site's bad week can pause every site.

**Findings (2026-11-12).** No DMARC record exists for anth.us or mail.machines-on-machines.anth.us; the SES pause alarm metrics were never tested on a live account; reputation is shared.

**Build.**
- DMARC as a template in Git (applied by the pipeline, no hand-made records): `_dmarc` for each sending domain starting at `p=none` with aggregate reports to a receiving mailbox, tightening to quarantine after reports show alignment; SPF and DKIM alignment verified per domain; MAIL FROM domain set.
- SES mailbox simulator tests as a repeatable drill: success, bounce, complaint, suppression-list, out-of-office, through the real site configuration set; verify the events reach EventBridge (PPY-819117), the ledger, suppression, and the pause alarm metrics.
- Pause drill: drive a bounce and complaint rate over the threshold in a test configuration set and watch the alarm pause only that site and the operator email arrive; then resume.
- Dead-letter reading: an operator procedure and alarm (PPY-e92c8e) for the email queue DLQ and router DLQ: what a stuck message looks like, how to replay or discard, who is told.
- Warm-up and seed-inbox plan: a schedule that grows volume from engaged recipients (learned from bounce and complaint data per step, no fixed ramp promised), a seed set of inboxes across Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo and Apple that we own, placement check before each step, a stop rule when complaints or bounces exceed the pause threshold. One-click List-Unsubscribe-Post honoured, Gmail bulk-sender rules checked.
- A readiness checklist that the MoM launch story reads: it passes or it does not.

**Specification.**
```gherkin
Feature: Deliverability readiness
  Scenario: DMARC published
    When the template is applied
    Then each sending domain has a DMARC record, aligned with SPF and DKIM, and a report mailbox receives aggregates

  Scenario: Simulator bounce
    When a message is sent to the SES bounce simulator through the site's set
    Then the address is suppressed and the event is recorded once

  Scenario: Simulator complaint
    Then the complaint is recorded and the reader is unsubscribed

  Scenario: Pause drill
    Given bounce and complaint rates above the site's threshold
    Then only that site's sending pauses and the operator is emailed

  Scenario: Dead letter
    Given a message in the email dead letter queue
    Then an alarm fires and the procedure shows how to replay or discard it

  Scenario: Warm-up step
    Given a warm-up step finished with complaint and bounce rates under the pause threshold and seed inboxes in the inbox
    Then the next step is allowed, otherwise it is held

  Scenario: Readiness gate
    When any item above is not done
    Then the readiness check fails and names it
```

**Depends on:** PPY-819117, PPY-c522bf. Blocks the MoM launch.
**Related:** PPY-e92c8e, PPY-f66e91, PPY-bf63d5, PPY-31455f constraints.

**Answered (Ryan, 2026-11-12):** (1) The DMARC report mailbox: none exists yet. Setting it up and publishing DMARC is PPY-6bcae9 (priority 1); it blocks this story and the MoM launch (PPY-f4b164). Ryan decides which mailbox or report service.

**Open questions for Ryan:** (1) Do we separate MoM onto its own SES account later, or accept shared reputation with these guardrails? (2) Who owns the seed inboxes?

comments.text: Decision (2026-11-12): the DMARC report mailbox does not exist yet. Filed PPY-6bcae9 (task, priority 1) to set it up and publish DMARC through the Git template; it blocks this story and PPY-f4b164. Ryan decides the mailbox. Questions 2 and 3 remain open.

comments.author: home
comments.text: PPY-1081ad adds a required step to this story: a forced pause drill on a test configuration set with the SES mailbox simulator (turn sending off, send to the simulator's success mailbox, record the exact error code, see the delivery failed with the pause reason; turn sending on, see the next send go out). PR #1427's SiteMailer recognises only SendingPausedException; a different code makes the delivery retry into the dead letter queue (alarmed, nothing sent). No site turns its public send path On before this passes. Documented in docs/plans/public-audiences.md and Caducus docs/public-audiences.md.
